interface.title: AMP Discovery — Antimicrobial Peptide Intelligence
interface.field: computational biology / peptide therapeutics (antimicrobial peptide discovery)
interface.stage_of_work: in-silico screening and triage of candidate sequences before wet-lab work
interface.what_it_is_for: Paste or load a peptide sequence and get an AMP/non-AMP call with probability, SHAP feature attributions, three-model agreement, a sequence-specific wet-lab assay plan, a what-if property simulator, and a downloadable feature CSV.

data.note: No upload exists anywhere in the UI. Input is the sequence text area plus a 'Load an example sequence...' dropdown with five built-ins (Magainin-2, LL-37 fragment, Indolicidin, Synthetic cationic AMP, Non-AMP control). Models (XGBoost/RF/LogReg) and the 1,586-sequence UniProt SwissProt training set are pre-shipped; nothing is fetched or trained at runtime.

tree.general: Decide whether a candidate molecule has the activity you are hunting for, understand why the model says so, and plan the bench work that would confirm it
tree.specific: Screen a peptide sequence for antimicrobial activity, see which physicochemical features drove the call, check model agreement, and leave with an assay plan and a feature CSV

features.name: Example-sequence loader that analyses on pick
features.general: A dropdown of curated reference items that fills the input and immediately runs the whole analysis, so a newcomer gets a full worked result in one click and can swap references to compare
features.specific: 'Load an example sequence...' with five built-ins (Magainin-2, LL-37 fragment, Indolicidin, Synthetic cationic AMP, Non-AMP control); picking one shows '✅ Loaded: …' and re-runs the prediction without pressing Analyze
steps: Open the example dropdown next to the Analyze button
Pick a reference peptide; the confirmation banner appears and the full result renders below
Swap to a different example to re-run everything on the new sequence, including a deliberate negative control
Reset the dropdown to the placeholder when you want your own typed sequence to be used instead — until you do, the dropdown silently overrides the text area
serves_tasks: start from a known reference item shipped with the tool
submit your own candidate instead of a built-in one

features.name: Verdict card with confidence band, property chips and property radar
features.general: A three-part result header that pairs a categorical call and its probability with the raw measurements behind it and a radar view of the single item's property profile
features.specific: Prediction panel (✅ AMP / ❌ non-AMP, % probability, fill bar, confidence wording) beside the residue-coloured sequence with length/charge/hydrophobicity/pI/fraction chips and a 5-axis radar (Hydrophobicity, Charge, Charge Density, Hydrophobic Fraction, Positive Fraction) for that one sequence
steps: Run a sequence and read the call plus its probability on the left card
Read the confidence wording, which degrades to 'Moderate — borderline sequence' near the cut-off
Scan the property chips and the colour-coded residues to see where charge and hydrophobicity come from
Open the radar fullscreen to read the profile axes for the analysed sequence
serves_tasks: read the call, its strength and how much to trust it
inspect the measured properties behind the call

features.name: SHAP driver panel (signed chart + ranked push-lists)
features.general: A per-item attribution view that shows which inputs pushed the answer toward or away from the positive class and by how much, as both a signed chart and two ranked lists, zoomable for close reading
features.specific: The SHAP Explanation tab: a two-colour horizontal bar chart (→ AMP green / → non-AMP red) around zero, with '↑ Driving toward AMP' and '↓ Driving toward non-AMP' lists of the top six features and their signed SHAP values
steps: Open the SHAP Explanation tab after analysing
Read the signed bar chart to see the direction and size of each feature's push
Read the two ranked lists for the exact values of the six strongest drivers each way
Click 'View fullscreen' to read the chart labels at full size
Analyse a second candidate and compare its driver ranking with the first
serves_tasks: see which measured features pushed the answer each way and by how much
compare what drives two different candidates

features.name: Three-model consensus comparator
features.general: A side-by-side comparison of independent methods scoring the same item, with a rolled-up agreement verdict — read with the caveat that the vote is counted at a different cut-off from the one drawn on the chart
features.specific: Model Consensus tab: bar chart of XGBoost / Random Forest / Logistic Regression probabilities with a dashed 'Decision threshold (0.5)' line and bars coloured by side of that line, plus a Consensus Summary (verdict, n/3 vote, average probability) and per-model value bars; the n/3 vote and verdict use OPTIMAL_THRESHOLD = 0.40, not the 0.5 line, so a bar below the line can still count as an AMP vote
steps: Open the Model Consensus tab for the analysed sequence
Read each model's probability against the dashed 0.5 line drawn on the chart
Read the Consensus Summary verdict, the n/3 model vote and the average probability, remembering the vote is taken at 0.40

Run a borderline sequence and watch a model fall between 0.40 and 0.5 — below the drawn line yet still counted in the unanimous vote; the 'Borderline — mixed signals' verdict appears only when the models split around 0.40
serves_tasks: compare several methods on one item and read the agreement summary
check how robust the answer is

features.name: Searchable feature table with CSV export
features.general: A full per-item measurement table you can filter in place and export as a file whose name carries the item's identity, so the numbers can be carried into other analysis
features.specific: Full Feature Report tab: a Feature / Value / Category table of 10 physicochemical plus 20 amino-acid-composition values, a built-in table search, and 'Download Feature Report (CSV)' producing amp_features_<first-10-residues>.csv
steps: Open the Full Feature Report tab
Scroll the table or use the search icon to filter, e.g. 'aa_' to isolate the 20 composition rows
Step through matches with the next/previous arrows
Press 'Download Feature Report (CSV)' and keep the sequence-named file
Repeat for another sequence to build a comparable set of exports
serves_tasks: browse and search the full table of computed values
download the per-item measurement table as a file

features.name: Conditional lab assay planner
features.general: A guidance panel that converts the item's measured properties into bench instructions, swapping each block's severity and wording as the properties cross thresholds, and pairing a standard protocol with a safety check
features.specific: Lab Assay Planner tab: Storage and Handling, Solubility and Dissolution and Proteolytic Stability blocks keyed to net charge, hydrophobic fraction and length, plus a CLSI M07-A10 / EUCAST broth microdilution protocol with priority ATCC strains and a hemolysis / therapeutic-index risk block
steps: Open the Lab Assay Planner tab after analysing
Read the storage block, which escalates to 'Surface Adhesion Risk' with BSA pre-coating advice for highly cationic sequences
Read the solubility block, which escalates from 'Moderate Hydrophobicity' to a 5-step DMSO dissolution protocol as hydrophobic fraction rises
Read the stability block, which flips from a caution to a green note as length increases
Copy the MIC protocol parameters and the three priority organisms into your plan
Read the hemolysis block and its HC50/MIC therapeutic-index targets before advancing the candidate
serves_tasks: read handling, dissolution and stability guidance conditioned on the item's measured properties
read the standard protocol and the safety check to run alongside it

features.name: Mutation playground (property sliders → approximated outcome → suggested edits)
features.general: A what-if panel whose sliders start at the item's own measured values and recompute an approximated outcome as you drag, wording the direction of travel and sometimes suggesting concrete next edits you can copy out; it is a linear attribution-weight approximation, not the real model, so its baseline does not match the headline probability and the signed 'Change' is not a like-for-like delta
features.specific: Mutation Playground tab: four sliders (Simulated Net Charge, Hydrophobic Fraction, Length, Positive Residue Fraction) pre-set to the sequence's values, three metric cards (Original / Simulated / Change), a progress bar, a ❌/🔁/✅ verdict block with a copy button, an 'Optimization Strategies Based On Your Sequence' block whose content varies by sequence (residue-position edits for some, a 'Strong candidate' note for others), and a disclaimer that it is a linear SHAP-weight approximation
steps: Open the Mutation Playground tab and note the sliders are seeded with this sequence's real values
Read Original vs Simulated before touching anything: they already differ (e.g. 74.9% vs 99.3%), so 'Change' does not start at zero
Drag one slider and read the Simulated Probability and signed Change as a relative trend only
Drag a second slider to see properties trade off (raising positive fraction up, raising hydrophobic fraction or length down)
Read the verdict block, which switches between 'decreased', 'minimal impact — try increasing charge above +4' and 'increased'
Read whatever 'Optimization Strategies' the sequence triggers, then press the copy button to take the verdict wording out of the app
serves_tasks: move each property control one at a time and watch the approximated outcome
read the plain-language verdict on the direction of travel and the suggested next edits

features.name: Training-data and validation scorecard
features.general: Two sidebar pages that let you audit what the predictions rest on before trusting them: the composition, class balance and declared bias of the reference collection, and a sortable table of cross-validated accuracy figures per method
features.specific: 📊 Dataset Info (1,586 UniProt SwissProt sequences, 793 AMP / 793 non-AMP, 10 biological sources, positive/negative source keyword lists and a 'Known Limitation' cysteine-bias note) and 🧠 Model Performance (5-fold CV table of accuracy, AUC-ROC, precision, recall and F1 for XGBoost / Random Forest / Logistic Regression, sortable by clicking a column header)
steps: Open 📊 Dataset Info from the sidebar and read the totals and class balance
Read the positive and negative source keyword lists and the 'Known Limitation' note on cysteine bias
Open 🧠 Model Performance and read the 5-fold CV metrics for all three models
Click a metric header (e.g. F1 Score) to reorder the models by the score you care about
Open 📖 About for the stack and the 'not validated for clinical use' disclaimer
serves_tasks: inspect the composition and known bias of the reference collection
compare the methods' accuracy figures and reorder them by whichever score matters
read the project's purpose, stack and limits of use

screens_never_reached: Per-slider help tooltips in the Mutation Playground — each slider carries a ⓘ/? icon, but hovering it produced no visible tooltip (screens/028.webp), so the intended wording was never seen.

A dedicated narrative 'biological explanation' panel — no such view exists as its own screen; biologically-worded prose is delivered inside the Lab Assay Planner and the Mutation Playground's verdict/strategies rather than beside the SHAP chart (screens/008.webp).
Any upload or batch-screening view — none is named or present anywhere in the UI; input is the text area and the example dropdown only.
The 'Borderline — mixed signals' consensus verdict — it requires the three models to split around the 0.40 vote cut-off, and no sequence tried produced that split.
not_done: Could not analyse a typed sequence while an example was still selected in the dropdown: the example overrides the text box, so Analyze re-ran the example instead (screens/033.webp, screens/034.webp). Workaround is to reset the dropdown to its placeholder first (screens/035.webp).

Could not keep a typed sequence's results on screen while using the result tabs' own controls: pressing the CSV download button or dragging a playground slider triggers a rerun that clears the whole analysis back to 'Enter a peptide sequence above to begin analysis' (screens/052.webp, screens/055.webp). Example-loaded sequences survive the same actions because the dropdown refills the input on rerun.
Results do not survive navigation: switching to Dataset Info / Model Performance / About and back to Predict empties the input and clears the analysis (screens/048.webp).
Could not drive the playground sliders from the keyboard: focusing a slider and pressing End left the value unchanged (screens/025.webp); only dragging worked.

Could not observe the stated 10–100 aa length limit being enforced on the built-in 'Non-AMP control', which is 294 aa and was analysed anyway (screens/031.webp), even though a typed 13 aa sequence with non-standard letters was rejected by the same rule text (screens/036.webp).

Could not find a sequence where the three models actually disagree on the call. The nearest was a borderline case where Random Forest scored 0.469 while the summary still reported 'Strong AMP — all models agree, 3/3' (screens/050.webp); that is consistent, not a bug, because the vote is counted at OPTIMAL_THRESHOLD = 0.40 while the chart line is drawn at 0.5. A true split needs a sequence where a model falls below 0.40, which was never found, so the disagreement-flagging path was never seen triggered.

The Mutation Playground's baseline does not match the real model: at the sequence's own unchanged slider values the simulated probability reads 74.9% against an original 99.3% (screens/064.webp), consistent with the panel's linear-approximation disclaimer but meaning the 'Change' figure is not a like-for-like delta and cannot be read as an absolute prediction.

The per-sequence 'Optimization Strategies' block is sequence-dependent and could not be reproduced on replay: the residue-position edits ('add K or R at positions 2, 5, 9') were seen for one typed sequence (screens/039.webp) while Magainin-2 showed a 'Strong candidate' note instead; that note also renders literal markdown asterisks.
